```{r setup, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>")
.opciones_previas <- options(width = 90, knitr.kable.NA = "—")
library(lupa)
num <- function(x) {
  format(x, big.mark = ".", decimal.mark = ",", scientific = FALSE, trim = TRUE)
}
codigo <- function(x) paste0("`", x, "`", collapse = ", ")
enumerar <- function(x) {
  x <- paste0("`", x, "`")
  if (length(x) < 2) return(x)
  paste(paste(x[-length(x)], collapse = ", "), "y", x[length(x)])
}
numero <- function(x, dec = 0L) {
  formatC(x, format = "f", digits = dec, big.mark = ".", decimal.mark = ",")
}
raiz_con <- function(...) {
  candidatas <- unique(c(file.path("..", ".."), getNamespaceInfo("lupa", "path")))
  hay <- file.exists(file.path(candidatas, ...))
  if (!any(hay)) stop("No se encuentra ", file.path(...), " en el paquete fuente.")
  candidatas[which(hay)[1L]]
}
raiz <- raiz_con("benchmark", "datos")
datos_banco <- file.path(raiz, "benchmark", "datos")
leer_banco <- function(nombre) {
  utils::read.csv(file.path(datos_banco, nombre), stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
}
interno <- function(nombre) get(nombre, envir = asNamespace("lupa"))
referencias_ancho <- leer_banco("medir-referencias.csv")
referencias_ancho <- referencias_ancho[
  referencias_ancho$escenario == "tabla_ancha", , drop = FALSE
]
referencias_ancho <- data.frame(
  n_columnas = referencias_ancho$n_columnas[referencias_ancho$medida == "perfilar"],
  segundos = referencias_ancho$valor[referencias_ancho$medida == "perfilar"],
  celdas_por_segundo = round(
    referencias_ancho$valor[referencias_ancho$medida == "celdas_por_segundo"]
  )
)
ancho_minima <- min(referencias_ancho$celdas_por_segundo)
archivos_codigos <- sort(
  list.files(
    datos_banco,
    pattern = "^medir-topes-valores-ancho-.*[.]csv$",
    full.names = TRUE
  ),
  decreasing = TRUE
)
if (!length(archivos_codigos)) stop("No encuentro el CSV de medir_topes_valores_ancho.R.")
codigos_ancho <- utils::read.csv(archivos_codigos[[1L]], stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
codigos_ancho <- codigos_ancho[codigos_ancho$escenario == "tabla_ancha", , drop = FALSE]
codigos_minima <- min(codigos_ancho$celdas_por_segundo)
dependencias <- function(campo) {
  x <- utils::packageDescription("lupa")[[campo]]
  x <- trimws(strsplit(x, ",")[[1]])
  x <- sub("\\s*\\(.*\\)$", "", x)
  x[nzchar(x)]
}
# The cost warnings with a threshold in seconds, read from the signature.
umbrales_aviso <- grep(
  "^umbral_segundos_aviso_", names(formals(perfilar_dbi)), value = TRUE
)
# The matrix of benchmark/verificar_motor.R: the names of `.especificaciones`,
# read from the script without running it.
guion_motores <- file.path(
  raiz_con("benchmark", "verificar_motor.R"), "benchmark", "verificar_motor.R"
)
matriz_guion <- NULL
for (expresion in parse(guion_motores, keep.source = FALSE)) {
  if (is.call(expresion) && identical(expresion[[1L]], as.name("<-")) &&
      identical(expresion[[2L]], as.name(".especificaciones"))) {
    matriz_guion <- names(as.list(expresion[[3L]]))[-1L]
  }
}
if (!length(matriz_guion)) {
  stop("benchmark/verificar_motor.R no define .especificaciones.")
}
```

> This guide is the English version of [Motores y escala](motores-y-escala.html).
> `lupa` writes its messages and tables in Spanish, so the output below,
> including the tables this page builds from the package, is in Spanish.

This page is the reference of `perfilar_dbi()` and `plan_perfilado_dbi()` for
whoever is going to profile a database in production:

- what is computed in the engine and what is brought into R;
- how much work each option asks for;
- what is declared;
- what is not estimated.

The walkthrough with an example is in
[Profiling a database](profiling-a-database.html). The help ships with the
package: `?perfilar_dbi`, `?plan_perfilado_dbi` and `?requisitos_motor`. It is
the complete source for each argument and each returned field.

The examples run against SQLite and DuckDB in memory every time the page is
built. What needs another engine is described without running it and with its
source.

## Default values {#defaults}

The table comes from the signatures of the 2 functions when this page is built.
A dash means that the function does not have that argument. For the arguments
that choose between options, the one that applies by default is shown and, in
parentheses, the others.

```{r valores, echo = FALSE}
opciones <- c("universo", "estrategia_mediana", "politica_costo", "bloque_muestra")
formatear <- function(nombre, valor) {
  if (is.null(valor)) return("`NULL`")
  if (nombre %in% opciones) {
    return(paste0(
      "`\"", valor[1], "\"` (", codigo(paste0("\"", valor[-1], "\"")), ")"
    ))
  }
  if (is.numeric(valor) && grepl("bytes", nombre) && length(valor) == 1 &&
      is.finite(valor) && valor > 0) {
    return(paste0("`", num(valor), "` (", valor / 1024^2, " MiB)"))
  }
  if (is.numeric(valor) && length(valor) == 1 && is.finite(valor) &&
      valor >= 1000) {
    return(paste0("`", num(valor), "`"))
  }
  paste0("`", paste(deparse(valor), collapse = ""), "`")
}
omisiones <- function(f) {
  fs <- formals(f)
  fs <- fs[setdiff(names(fs), c("conexion", "tabla", "..."))]
  vapply(names(fs), function(n) {
    formatear(n, eval(fs[[n]], asNamespace("lupa")))
  }, character(1))
}
en_corrida <- omisiones(perfilar_dbi)
en_plan <- omisiones(plan_perfilado_dbi)
argumentos <- union(names(en_corrida), names(en_plan))
tabla_omisiones <- data.frame(
  argumento = paste0("`", argumentos, "`"),
  corrida = ifelse(argumentos %in% names(en_corrida), en_corrida[argumentos], "—"),
  plan = ifelse(argumentos %in% names(en_plan), en_plan[argumentos], "—")
)
names(tabla_omisiones) <- c("argumento", "`perfilar_dbi()`", "`plan_perfilado_dbi()`")
knitr::kable(tabla_omisiones, row.names = FALSE)
```

Consequences for a run in production:

- With `universo = "tabla_completa"` (*universe = whole table*) and
  `muestra = Inf` (*sample*), the SQL aggregates go through the whole table.
  With those same values, the block `perfil_muestra` (*sample profile*) tries to
  bring into R **all** the rows that `max_celdas_muestra` and
  `max_bytes_muestra` allow.
  `muestra` bounds only that read, never the aggregates. To bound the work of
  the engine there is `universo = "muestra_motor"` (*engine sample*); to bring
  no rows, `bloque_muestra = "solo_agregados"` (*sample block = aggregates
  only*).
- `instrumentar` (*instrument*) is `TRUE` in `perfilar_dbi()` and `FALSE` in
  the plan: the run times each query and the plan does not.
- `perfil_muestra` is computed with `perfilar()` on the rows brought in, with
  `muestra = Inf` and no caps of its own. The caps were already applied when
  reading. That is why the discovery of patterns, types and dates goes through
  all those rows. `perfilar()` in memory, instead, does it by default on a
  sample of `r chartr(".,", ",.", num(eval(formals(perfilar)$muestra)))` rows.
  The other arguments of `perfilar()` arrive through `...`.

  In `universo = "muestra_motor"`, the materialization is bounded before
  `dbFetch(n)` with a conservative bound on the maximum row size. Long texts
  are requested as length and summary: that way their content cannot make the
  fetch exceed that bound. A type without a safe bound is probed one row at a
  time. The part that fits is kept if the budget runs out. A cut, a short
  final sample or a query failure leaves metadata and emits
  `lupa_aviso_muestra_motor`.

## What is computed in the engine and what is brought into R {#universes}

`perfilar_dbi()` returns an object of class `perfil_dbi` with 2 blocks. They
come from different universes and do not replace each other:

- `resumen_tabla` (*table summary*): SQL aggregates that the engine computes
  (counts, completeness, cardinality, mode, extremes, mean, median, standard
  deviation). It carries one row per column and metric in `resumen_tabla$sql`.
- `perfil_muestra`: the full profile of `perfilar()` on the rows brought into
  R, with its findings and its coverage of diagnostics.

What goes into each block is decided by 4 arguments:

| argument | decides |
| --- | --- |
| `universo` | on which rows the engine computes the aggregates: the whole table (`"tabla_completa"`) or a selection made by the engine itself (`"muestra_motor"`, with `muestra_motor = n` required) |
| `muestra` | how many rows are brought into R for `perfil_muestra`; `Inf` brings all the ones the caps allow |
| `orden_muestra` (*sample order*) | which rows are brought and whether the read is reproducible |
| `bloque_muestra` | whether any row is brought (`"con_muestra"`, *with sample*) or only the aggregates are computed (`"solo_agregados"`) |

The usual combinations:

| configuration | SQL aggregates (`resumen_tabla`) | rows brought into R (`perfil_muestra`) |
| --- | --- | --- |
| default | the whole table | all the ones `max_celdas_muestra` and `max_bytes_muestra` allow |
| `muestra = n` | the whole table | up to `n`: the first ones the engine returns, or the first ones by `orden_muestra` |
| `universo = "muestra_motor"`, `muestra_motor = n` | up to `n` rows selected by the engine | the rows actually materialized, cut by `muestra` and the caps |
| `bloque_muestra = "solo_agregados"` | whatever `universo` says | none: `perfil_muestra` is `NULL` and the coverage says `no_solicitado` (*not requested*) |

`bloque_muestra = "solo_agregados"` is independent of `universo`. With
`muestra_motor`, the aggregates still use the selection of the engine, but no
rows are selected, read or kept in the client:

- `meta$materializacion$estado` says `no_solicitado`;
- `meta$bloques$filas_vistas` is 0.

The example uses a table of 2,000 rows in SQLite in memory.

```{r tabla-ejemplo}
con <- DBI::dbConnect(RSQLite::SQLite(), ":memory:")
set.seed(11)
n <- 2000
tramites <- data.frame(
  id_tramite = seq_len(n),
  categoria = sample(c("A", "B", "C", "D"), n, replace = TRUE),
  monto = round(stats::rlnorm(n, 9, 1.1), 2),
  edad = c(sample(18:85, n - 20, replace = TRUE), rep(NA, 20))
)
DBI::dbWriteTable(con, "tramites", tramites)
```

```{r cuatro-configuraciones}
por_omision <- perfilar_dbi(con, "tramites")
con_muestra <- perfilar_dbi(con, "tramites", muestra = 500, orden_muestra = "id_tramite")
del_motor <- perfilar_dbi(con, "tramites", universo = "muestra_motor", muestra_motor = 300)
solo_agregados <- perfilar_dbi(con, "tramites", bloque_muestra = "solo_agregados")

alcance <- function(x) {
  r <- x$resumen_tabla
  data.frame(
    universo = r$meta$universo,
    n_resumen = r$columnas$n[r$columnas$columna == "id_tramite"],
    validos_resumen = r$columnas$n_validos[r$columnas$columna == "id_tramite"],
    filas_en_r = if (is.null(x$perfil_muestra)) 0 else n_filas(x$perfil_muestra)
  )
}
rbind(
  por_omision = alcance(por_omision),
  con_muestra = alcance(con_muestra),
  del_motor = alcance(del_motor),
  solo_agregados = alcance(solo_agregados)
)
```

```{r comprobar-universos, echo = FALSE}
stopifnot(
  identical(por_omision$resumen_tabla$meta$universo, "tabla_completa"),
  n_filas(por_omision$perfil_muestra) == n,
  n_filas(con_muestra$perfil_muestra) == 500,
  identical(del_motor$resumen_tabla$meta$universo, "muestra_motor"),
  is.null(solo_agregados$perfil_muestra),
  # The 2 blocks that the text names above are the whole object.
  identical(names(por_omision), c("resumen_tabla", "perfil_muestra"))
)
```

The metric `n` always keeps the total of the table, also with `muestra_motor`.
The other SQL metrics of that universe are observations of the selection of the
engine, not extrapolations to the universe.

`resumen_tabla$columnas` carries
`r ncol(por_omision$resumen_tabla$columnas) - 1` fields per column;
`perfil_muestra`, the full profile of `perfilar()`, carries
`r ncol(columnas(por_omision$perfil_muestra)) - 1`. The accessors
`hallazgos()`, `columnas()`, `cobertura()`, `n_filas()` and `sql_perfil()`
work on both kinds of object. Their contract is in
[Leer un perfil](leer-un-perfil.html) (*Reading a profile*, in Spanish).

Without a sample, the protection of personal data, if requested, cannot
classify the columns. It then protects the cell values of all of them: mode,
extremes, mean, median and standard deviation stay `omitido_por_privacidad`
(*omitted for privacy*).

```{r sin-muestra-protegido}
con_proteccion <- perfilar_dbi(
  con, "tramites", bloque_muestra = "solo_agregados",
  proteger_datos_personales = TRUE
)
table(sql_perfil(con_proteccion)$estado)
table(sql_perfil(solo_agregados)$estado)
```

With a sample, the classification is done on `perfil_muestra` and also reaches
the summary. The detail of what is masked is in
[Alcance y cobertura](https://sebollin.github.io/lupa/articles/alcance-y-cobertura.html)
(*Scope and coverage*, in Spanish).

## Sampling metadata: 2 paths {#metadata}

There are 2 places with sampling metadata, and they describe different things:

| path | exists when | describes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `perfil_muestra$meta$origen_dbi$muestreo` | the block of rows was requested and read (`bloque_muestra = "con_muestra"`), with any `universo` | the read into R: `filas_solicitadas`, `filas_obtenidas`, `acotado_en`, `metodo`, `reproducible` and the statement `sql_muestra` |
| `resumen_tabla$meta$muestreo` | only with `universo = "muestra_motor"` | the selection of the engine: `metodo_muestreo`, `sesgo_muestreo`, `tamano_muestra`, `fraccion`, `universo` and the identifiers of the local copy |

In the usual case —`tabla_completa` with `muestra`— the second path is `NULL`.
A script that reads it out of habit, without checking for `NULL`, computes on
nothing:

```{r rutas-tabla-completa}
is.null(con_muestra$resumen_tabla$meta$muestreo)
lectura <- con_muestra$perfil_muestra$meta$origen_dbi$muestreo
str(lectura[c("filas_solicitadas", "filas_obtenidas", "acotado_en", "metodo",
              "reproducible")])
```

With `muestra_motor` both paths show up, and their sizes answer different
questions:

- `filas_obtenidas`, from the read into R: how many rows `perfilar()` received;
- `tamano_muestra`, from the selection of the engine: how many the engine query
  asked for.

```{r rutas-muestra-motor}
seleccion <- del_motor$resumen_tabla$meta$muestreo
str(seleccion[c("metodo_muestreo", "sesgo_muestreo", "tamano_muestra",
                "fraccion", "universo", "filas_obtenidas")])
```

```{r comprobar-rutas, echo = FALSE}
stopifnot(
  is.null(por_omision$resumen_tabla$meta$muestreo),
  is.null(con_muestra$resumen_tabla$meta$muestreo),
  !is.null(con_muestra$perfil_muestra$meta$origen_dbi$muestreo),
  !is.null(del_motor$resumen_tabla$meta$muestreo),
  lectura$filas_obtenidas == 500,
  seleccion$tamano_muestra == 300
)
```

In `resumen_tabla$meta$muestreo`:

- `tamano_muestra`: the effective size requested from the query;
- `filas_solicitadas`: the original request;
- `filas_pedidas`: the request after the caps;
- `filas_obtenidas`: the rows that the local copy returned.

If `muestra` is smaller than `muestra_motor`, `meta$materializacion$n_filas` can
exceed `n_filas(perfil_muestra)`.

The cardinality of a sample is published with status `observado_muestra`
(*observed in the sample*). It is what was seen in the sample, with the universe
next to it. It does not estimate the one of the universe without a declared
estimator.

Without `orden_muestra`, the rows brought are the first ones the engine
returns, in an order that SQL does not guarantee. `reproducible` says so. With
`orden_muestra`, the read is declared reproducible only if the combination of
columns is unique in the whole table. The package checks it
(`orden_unico_verificado`).

## Sampling forms in the engine {#sampling-forms}

With `universo = "muestra_motor"`, the selection is made by the engine with the
first form that its dialect offers and its probe accepts. The order is fixed in
the code:

| order | form | offered to | size obtained |
| ---: | --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | `TABLESAMPLE RESERVOIR (n ROWS)` | DuckDB | exactly `n` rows |
| 2 | `TABLESAMPLE SYSTEM (p)` | PostgreSQL, SQL Server | whole blocks: it varies around the request and can give 0 rows in a small table |
| 3 | `TABLESAMPLE BERNOULLI (p)` (in DuckDB, `(p PERCENT)`: there a bare number is a row count) | PostgreSQL, DuckDB | row by row: it varies little around the request, at the price of going through the table |
| 4 | `TABLESAMPLE (p PERCENT)` | SQL Server | by pages |
| 5 | `SAMPLE (p)` | Oracle | row by row |
| 6 | pseudorandom order with the limit of the dialect | any engine with a limit | exactly `n`, at the price of sorting the whole table |

```{r comprobar-orden-muestreo, echo = FALSE}
orden_documentado <- c(
  "tablesample_reservoir", "tablesample_system", "tablesample_bernoulli",
  "tablesample_percent", "random_limit"
)
stopifnot(identical(lupa:::.dialectos_dbi()$limit$muestreo, orden_documentado))
```

The fixed-quantity form goes first because 2 queries of the same profile must
see samples of comparable size. The block forms cost less on large tables, and
that is why they come before the row-by-row ones. But their size jumps. DuckDB
lets it be seen on the same table of 5,000 rows, asking for 20% with 6 seeds:

```{r tamanos-de-muestra}
duck <- suppressMessages(DBI::dbConnect(duckdb::duckdb()))
DBI::dbWriteTable(duck, "t", data.frame(id = seq_len(5000)))
contar <- function(muestreo, semillas = 1:6) {
  vapply(semillas, function(s) {
    sql <- paste("SELECT COUNT(*) FROM t TABLESAMPLE", sprintf(muestreo, s))
    DBI::dbGetQuery(duck, sql)[[1]]
  }, numeric(1))
}
tamanos <- rbind(
  bloques = contar("20 PERCENT (system, %d)"),
  fila_por_fila = contar("20 PERCENT (bernoulli, %d)"),
  cantidad_fija = contar("RESERVOIR (1000 ROWS) REPEATABLE (%d)")
)
colnames(tamanos) <- paste0("semilla_", 1:6)
tamanos
```

Out of 1,000 rows requested:

- block sampling gave between
  `r chartr(".,", ",.", num(min(tamanos["bloques", ])))` and
  `r chartr(".,", ",.", num(max(tamanos["bloques", ])))`;
- row-by-row sampling, between
  `r chartr(".,", ",.", num(min(tamanos["fila_por_fila", ])))` and
  `r chartr(".,", ",.", num(max(tamanos["fila_por_fila", ])))`;
- fixed-quantity sampling, always
  `r chartr(".,", ",.", num(unique(tamanos["cantidad_fija", ])))`.

What each form implies is published:

- `TABLESAMPLE SYSTEM` publishes `sesgo_muestreo = "por_bloques"` (*sampling
  bias = by blocks*) with the reason
  `sesgo_muestreo:tablesample_system_por_bloques`. If it receives 0 rows or less
  than half of the requested ones, a broader form is tried once. The methods,
  the retry and the rows obtained stay in `resumen_tabla$meta$muestreo`. If the
  retry reaches the request, no warning is emitted. Only the short final sample
  stays `no_disponible` (*not available*) with
  `muestra_inestable:tablesample_system_tamano_insuficiente` and emits the
  degradation warning.
- The pseudorandom order publishes `sesgo_muestreo = "por_fila"` (*by row*). In
  SQL Server, where the function is `NEWID()`, the median under `muestra_motor`
  only accepts that form if:

  - the table has up to `r chartr(".,", ",.", num(lupa:::.MAX_FILAS_NEWID_DBI))`
    rows;
  - the requested sample is at least
    `r 100 * lupa:::.MIN_FRACCION_NEWID_DBI`% of the table;
  - the projection, of `r lupa:::.TASA_NEWID_MS_POR_MILLON_DBI` ms per million
    rows per pending median, does not go over
    `r chartr(".,", ",.", num(lupa:::.MAX_PROYECCION_NEWID_MS_DBI))` ms.

  They are constants of the code, not measurements of the run. Outside those
  limits, the median stays `no_disponible` with
  `capacidad_no_aceptada:newid_costo_excede_presupuesto`.
- If no form is accepted, the SQL metrics stay `no_disponible`. They are never
  replaced by results of the whole table.
- If the sample comes back empty, the metrics with scope `muestra` are published
  as `NA` with status `no_disponible` and a reason `muestra_vacia:...`. Zero is
  not published, and the column is not concluded to be empty.

## Caps on the read into R {#caps}

`perfil_muestra` has 2 caps, which do not touch any aggregate query:

- `max_celdas_muestra`
  (`r chartr(".,", ",.", num(lupa:::.MAX_CELDAS_MUESTRA))` cells by default) is
  resolved **before reading**, with the row count and the width of the schema.
- `max_bytes_muestra` (`r lupa:::.MAX_BYTES_MUESTRA / 1024^2` MiB by default)
  is crossed with the budget of the spool. In the engines that allow it, it
  uses the catalog. In the others, it starts with a small block and adapts
  `dbFetch(n)`. The sample is not brought in whole to be cut in R. Measured in
  PostgreSQL 16 and SQL Server: 200 rows with a text of a million characters
  and a 250 KB binary (250 and 300 MB) reach the spool in 27 KB, each long
  value as its length and its MD5; with `max_bytes_muestra = 1e6` on 2,000
  texts of 9,000 characters, 109 rows are read, 0.99 MB, and
  `meta$materializacion$tope_que_mando` is `"bytes"`.

If `muestra = n` and a cap is stricter, the smaller one rules. The coverage of
diagnostics of `perfil_muestra` declares the cells or bytes observed, the
threshold and which cap ruled. `Inf` in a cap turns it off. With a cap of 1,000
cells on 4 columns:

```{r tope-de-celdas}
acotado <- perfilar_dbi(con, "tramites", max_celdas_muestra = 1000)
str(acotado$perfil_muestra$meta$origen_dbi$muestreo[c(
  "filas_solicitadas", "filas_maximas_por_celdas", "celdas_solicitadas",
  "filas_obtenidas", "acotado_en"
)])
"muestra_perfilado" %in% cobertura(acotado$perfil_muestra)$diagnostico
```

`plan_perfilado_dbi()` anticipates the cut of cells in
`attr(plan, "tope_muestra")` and warns that the one of bytes will need the
probe.

The work is governed by 4 other limits:

| argument | what it bounds | when it runs out |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `max_consultas` | number of queries of the run | the remaining metrics stay `no_disponible` and the coverage says `presupuesto_agotado` (*budget exhausted*) |
| `max_bytes_materializacion` | bytes of the local copy of `muestra_motor`, bounded before each `dbFetch(n)` and checked before each write | `spool_presupuesto_excedido` and `muestra_inestable:presupuesto_materializacion`; the part that fit is kept |
| `max_bytes_procesamiento` | state retained by the read in blocks and by the reread of the local copy | if the object exceeds the limit, the sample is discarded with `lupa_aviso_muestra_motor` and `tope_que_mando = "procesamiento"` is published |
| `bloque_filas` | turns on the pass through the whole table in blocks of that size | — |

`bloque_filas = n` (*row block*) computes in R the summary of the whole table,
without retaining all the rows. It reads the table in blocks of `n` rows from a
single result set (`dbSendQuery()` and `dbFetch(n)`). The coverage is read in
`meta$bloques$filas_vistas`. `perfil_muestra` is still the diagnostic sample
bounded by `muestra` and the caps. The drivers without proven incremental
retention —DuckDB among them— stay `no_disponible` with their reason and a
warning `lupa_aviso_muestra_motor`.

```{r por-bloques}
por_bloques <- perfilar_dbi(con, "tramites", bloque_filas = 500, muestra = 100)
por_bloques$resumen_tabla$meta$bloques$filas_vistas
n_filas(por_bloques$perfil_muestra)
```

## Caps on the approximate comparison {#duplicate-caps}

The caps of `detectar_duplicados_aproximados()` (*detect approximate
duplicates*) and of the vocabulary diagnostic cut work in R. They do not cut
the queries that an engine already ran. This example recreates the table of
suppliers of
[Escala y duplicados](escala-y-duplicados.html#un-registro-de-proveedores)
(*Scale and approximate duplicates*, in Spanish) so that each output is
independent.

```{r duplicados-datos, include = FALSE}
proveedores <- data.frame(
  id = 1:8,
  proveedor = c(
    "Ferretería Central", "Ferreteria Central", "Distribuidora Sur",
    "Distribuidora Sur", "Lácteos del Este", "Lacteos del Este",
    "Imprenta Norte", "Imprenta Nortes"
  ),
  rubro = c(
    "ferretería", "ferretería", "alimentos", "alimentos", "alimentos",
    "alimentos", "gráfica", "gráfica"
  ),
  anio_alta = c(2022, 2022, 2021, 2021, 2020, 2020, NA, NA),
  stringsAsFactors = FALSE
)
pares <- detectar_duplicados_aproximados(
  proveedores, columnas = c("proveedor", "rubro")
)
ajustado <- perfilar(
  proveedores, analizar_dependencias = FALSE, max_trabajo_vocabulario = 2000
)
```

### The length of the values

A normalized distance loses its power to tell values apart when the texts are
long. The measure of the detector is Jaro-Winkler with `p = 0.1`. It shows with
2 texts that differ in exactly 100 characters, at different lengths.

```{r distancia-largo}
distancia_cien_cambios <- function(largo, semilla) {
  set.seed(semilla)
  texto <- sample(letters, largo, replace = TRUE)
  otro <- texto
  cambios <- sample(largo, 100)
  otro[cambios] <- ifelse(otro[cambios] == "a", "b", "a")
  stringdist::stringdist(
    paste(texto, collapse = ""), paste(otro, collapse = ""),
    method = "jw", p = 0.1
  )
}
largos <- c(500, 1000, 2000, 4000, 8000)
data.frame(
  largo = largos,
  distancia = vapply(largos, function(largo) {
    round(median(vapply(1:5, distancia_cien_cambios, numeric(1), largo = largo)), 3)
  }, numeric(1))
)
```

The 100 differences are the same: what changes is how much they weigh in the
text. Past a certain length, the distance drops below the threshold of 0.10.
Then 2 texts that differ in 100 characters count as almost equal.

That is why the detector does not compare values longer than `max_largo_valor`
(*maximum value length*;
`r chartr(".,", ",.", num(pares$alcance$max_largo_valor))` characters by
default, an assumption of the code). The cap does not remove the effect, it
bounds it: a column of long texts can ask for a smaller one. It is measured on
the string that is really compared, with the columns already joined and
normalized. If it is exceeded, the whole combination stays out of scope and is
declared. With a cap of 20 characters, the string of supplier and line of
business does not fit:

```{r largo}
corto <- detectar_duplicados_aproximados(
  proveedores, columnas = c("proveedor", "rubro"), max_largo_valor = 20
)
corto$alcance[, c(
  "max_largo_valor", "largo_maximo", "columnas_excluidas_largo", "n_pares_hallados"
)]
```

```{r largo-cifras, include = FALSE}
stopifnot(nrow(corto$pares) == 0L)
```

`largo_maximo` is the length of the compared string, not the one of each
column. `n_pares_hallados` is `NA`, not zero: nothing was compared. With
`max_largo_valor = Inf` there is no cap and no length is measured: that field is
`NA`, not zero.

The vocabulary diagnostic of `perfilar()` has its own cap,
`max_largo_valor_vocabulario`, which is not inherited. The one of the detector
is passed with `perfilar(duplicados_aproximados = list(max_largo_valor = ...))`.
In `perfilar()`, the same cap also declares the coverage of the costly text
operations that are not run on those values.

### The vocabulary work in `perfilar()`

`perfilar()` looks for nearly identical variants within each text column
(`casi_duplicados_vocabulario`, *near-duplicate vocabulary*), comparing their
distinct values in pairs. Comparing 2 values of lengths `L1` and `L2` costs on
the order of `L1 × L2`. That is why the budget, `max_trabajo_vocabulario`, is
measured in character comparisons: `2e10` by default. When it falls short, it
compares the first forms in alphabetical order —not a sample— and declares the
rest. With a minimal budget it shows:

```{r vocabulario}
recorte <- cobertura(ajustado)
recorte <- recorte[recorte$diagnostico == "proximidad_vocabulario", ]
writeLines(strwrap(paste0(recorte$columna, ": ", recorte$motivo), 88))
```

```{r vocabulario-cifras, include = FALSE}
stopifnot(
  eval(formals(perfilar)$max_trabajo_vocabulario) == 2e10,
  eval(formals(perfilar)$max_trabajo_dependencias) == 1e8,
  eval(formals(detectar_duplicados_aproximados)$max_resultados) == 100
)
```

The alphabetical order makes the result independent of the order of the rows of
the file. The search for dependencies has its own budget:
`max_trabajo_dependencias`, of `1e8` row-pair comparisons by default. `Inf`
turns off either of the 2.

### How many pairs are returned

`max_resultados` (100 by default) does not decide what is compared, but how many
pairs are returned: it keeps the closest ones. With a cut of 2, on the 3 pairs
at distance 0:

```{r empate}
dos <- detectar_duplicados_aproximados(
  proveedores, columnas = c("proveedor", "rubro"), max_resultados = 2
)
dos$pares[, c("fila_1", "fila_2", "distancia", "tipo_par")]
dos$alcance[, c("truncado", "distancia_corte", "corte_en_empate")]
```

`corte_en_empate = TRUE` (*cut in a tie*) warns that at least one pair **as
close** as the kept ones was left out. It is not `truncado` (*truncated*) under
another name: if the cut falls on a unique distance, it is `FALSE` even if
something was cut. To bring all the tied ones, `max_resultados` has to go up.

Among tied pairs, the tie-break uses the content of the values and not the
position of the rows. Reordering the table does not change which pairs stay:

```{r empate-orden}
ids_conservados <- function(datos, resultado) {
  a <- datos$id[resultado$pares$fila_1]
  b <- datos$id[resultado$pares$fila_2]
  sort(paste(pmin(a, b), pmax(a, b), sep = "-"))
}
invertidos <- proveedores[8:1, ]
dos_invertidos <- detectar_duplicados_aproximados(
  invertidos, columnas = c("proveedor", "rubro"), max_resultados = 2
)
ids_conservados(proveedores, dos)
ids_conservados(invertidos, dos_invertidos)
```

## ⚠️ What the SQL aggregates do not translate {#not-translated}

`sentinelas_numericos`, `aplicabilidad` and `columnas_opcionales` (*numeric
sentinels*, *applicability*, *optional columns*) change what `perfil_muestra`
summarizes. The SQL aggregates are computed without them: `AVG()` knows nothing
of sentinels. When any of them is declared, `resumen_tabla$cobertura` receives
a `degradado` (*degraded*) row that says so. With 30 ages `-999` declared as a
sentinel, the 2 blocks publish 2 different means on the same rows:

```{r centinelas}
centinelas <- tramites
centinelas$edad[1:30] <- -999L
DBI::dbWriteTable(con, "centinelas", centinelas)
declarado <- perfilar_dbi(con, "centinelas", sentinelas_numericos = -999)

media_edad <- function(cols) cols$media[cols$columna == "edad"]
c(
  resumen_sql = media_edad(columnas(declarado)),
  perfil_muestra = media_edad(columnas(declarado$perfil_muestra))
)
cobertura(declarado)[, c("bloque", "elemento", "estado")]
```

On a `perfil_dbi`, `columnas()` returns those of the SQL summary. Those of the
sample profile are requested on `perfil_muestra`.

When the 2 blocks exist, `perfilar_dbi()` crosses them. It compares only what
both measure with the same semantics. What a declaration changes on purpose
stays in `meta$corroboracion_bloques$no_comparadas`, with its cause:

```{r no-comparadas}
head(declarado$resumen_tabla$meta$corroboracion_bloques$no_comparadas, 4)
```

If 2 comparable values differ beyond the tolerance, the coverage receives a
`divergencia` (*divergence*) row with the 2 values. No winner is chosen. If the
sample covers only part of the table, an ordinary difference is to be expected:
it is declared `no_corroborada` (*not corroborated*), not `divergencia`.

The tolerance is in `meta$corroboracion_bloques$tolerancia`:

- for the values read, `1e-10` absolute plus 64 machine epsilons relative;
- for the mean and the standard deviation, which each side accumulates in its
  own way, `1e-10` relative.

`columnas_codigo` (*code columns*), which arrives through `...`, does apply to
the summary. The mean, the median and the standard deviation of a declared
column stay `NA`, and the coverage marks them `no_aplica` (*does not apply*).

## Metrics and strategies {#metrics}

`metricas` (*metrics*) chooses groups; each group publishes these fields of
`resumen_tabla$columnas`:

```{r grupos-de-metricas, echo = FALSE}
grupos <- lupa:::.CAMPOS_METRICA_DBI
knitr::kable(data.frame(
  grupo = paste0("`\"", names(grupos), "\"`"),
  campos = vapply(grupos, codigo, character(1))
), row.names = FALSE)
```

`metricas = c("validos", "basicos", "desvio")` avoids the cardinality, the mode
and the median, which are the queries that group or sort.
`metricas = "validos"` leaves only completeness.

Each row of `resumen_tabla$sql` carries `estado`, `alcance`, `universo`,
`tamano_muestra`, `fraccion`, `metodo` and `error_esperado`. `estado` tells
apart what was computed, what was estimated and what is not available, besides
what was omitted for cost or for protection. In an engine sample,
`error_esperado` (*expected error*) is:

- `no_estimado` (*not estimated*) when the error could be computed under a
  probabilistic design, but was not computed;
- `no_estimable` (*not estimable*) for the mode, the median and the observed
  cardinality;
- `no_aplica` when there was no effective sampling.

No numeric bound is published without a formula that justifies it.

**`estrategia_distintos`** (*distinct-count strategy*) chooses where
`n_distintos` comes from:

- `"exacta"` (*exact*, the default): `COUNT(DISTINCT)` on the rows of the run.
- `"aproximada_motor"` (*engine approximation*): a native function, only if the
  probe accepts it. Its undocumented error bounds stay as `"desconocido"`
  (*unknown*). If the function only knows how to build a full query, valid and
  distinct values are emitted separately. Each record keeps the method of the
  query that ran.
- `"catalogo"` (*catalog*): `pg_stats.n_distinct` of PostgreSQL, published as
  `estimado_catalogo` (*catalog estimate*), only with
  `universo = "tabla_completa"`.
- `"omitida"` (*omitted*): it does not emit the query.

There is no fallback between strategies: a strategy without the capability
stays `no_disponible` and is never turned into an exact count. In SQLite, the
catalog does not exist:

```{r distintos-catalogo}
por_catalogo <- perfilar_dbi(
  con, "tramites", estrategia_distintos = "catalogo",
  bloque_muestra = "solo_agregados"
)
estrategia <- por_catalogo$resumen_tabla$meta$estrategia_distintos
estrategia$estado
writeLines(strwrap(estrategia$motivo, 88))
```

What was requested, what was resolved and the status stay in
`meta$estrategia_distintos` and in the columns `estrategia_solicitada` and
`estrategia_resuelta` of `resumen_tabla$sql`.

**`estrategia_mediana`** (*median strategy*) enables an approximation, but does
not impose it. The probe tries in this order:

1. a consolidated exact form;
2. an exact one per column;
3. the approximate ones, at the end.

`resumen_tabla$sql$metodo` says what ran. Only an approximation that was run
stays `estimado` (*estimated*). `universo = "muestra_motor"` with
`estrategia_mediana = "aproximada_motor"` is rejected on entry.

**`incluir_valores = FALSE`** (*include values*) does not emit the queries of
mode, extremes and median. It also clears the cell values of the summary, the
sample, the blocks, the coverage and the reasons. An engine error message,
which quotes the cell that caused it, is published without its literals, as
with protection on. Counts and proportions are still published.

## Batched queries {#batches}

The cost of a large table is the number of passes, not the sampling. That is
why the queries are grouped:

- **Flat aggregates**: `COUNT(col)`, minimum, maximum, mean, zeros, negatives
  and standard deviation. They travel in a single query per batch of up to
  `tamano_lote_planos` (*flat batch size*) columns
  (`r lupa:::.TAMANO_LOTE_PLANOS_DBI` by default). In SQL Server and for
  `float8` of PostgreSQL, the standard deviation adds a second query per batch.
  That way it keeps the centered computation. Each query brings
  `COUNT(*) AS n_total_consulta`: completeness uses that local denominator and
  not the total of another batch. The mean and the standard deviation of the
  decimal columns are also requested in one query per batch of up to
  `tamano_lote_planos` columns: the sum and the sum of the squares of the
  differences from the mean, in the column's type. If the engine rejects a
  batch, it is split until the column is isolated. On the engine sample those
  sums go in the batch of aggregates, in the same statement.
- **Exact cardinalities** go in their own class, in batches of
  `tamano_lote_distintos` (*distinct batch size*;
  `r lupa:::.TAMANO_LOTE_DISTINTOS_DBI` by default). Each
  `COUNT(DISTINCT col)` travels with `COUNT(col) AS n_validos_guard`, a control
  count of the same statement.
- **The mode** is one query per column, because it groups. It tries to bring
  `SUM(COUNT(*)) OVER () AS n_validos_guard` along with its frequency. The form
  is probed. If the engine rejects it, the query without that count is used and
  `resumen_tabla$meta$moda_guardian` declares it.
- **The median** is one query per column as a fallback. If the probe accepts
  `PERCENTILE_CONT(...) WITHIN GROUP` and the percentile returns its full
  digits, several travel in a single `SELECT` per batch. The test asks for a row
  with a value above 1e8 and another below 1e-10, which have to come back
  identical. In SQL Server that requires compatibility level 110 or higher.
  Decimal columns do not go in that `SELECT`: their median is the sum of their
  middle values, one query per column. With `bloque_filas`, the mean of the
  decimal columns is one more query for all of them, and their median, when the
  two middle values fall on different doubles, one sorted query per column.
  MariaDB accepts the form, but returns the percentile with 10 decimals and a
  cap at 1e8: it uses the median per column, like MySQL. The reason for a
  rejection stays in `meta$mediana_consolidada$motivo`.
- In the dialects with `LIMIT` that do not have `PERCENTILE_CONT`, like SQLite
  and PostgreSQL 9.3, the count of the median goes in a scalar subquery of the
  same statement. For that, the probe has to accept integer division with `%`
  and `/`.

`tamano_lote` sets both sizes at once. The number of queries that each size
produces on the table of the example, according to the plan:

```{r lotes}
consultas_por_lote <- function(...) {
  plan <- plan_perfilado_dbi(con, "tramites", ...)
  tabla <- as.data.frame(plan)
  c(
    planos = sum(tabla$n_consultas[grepl("planos", tabla$clase_consulta)]),
    distintos = sum(tabla$n_consultas[grepl("distintos", tabla$clase_consulta)]),
    total = attr(plan, "total")
  )
}
rbind(
  planos_1 = consultas_por_lote(tamano_lote_planos = 1),
  por_omision = consultas_por_lote(),
  distintos_1 = consultas_por_lote(tamano_lote_distintos = 1),
  distintos_4 = consultas_por_lote(tamano_lote_distintos = 4)
)
```

The value of `tamano_lote_distintos` is an assumption of the code, noted next to
the constant (`R/perfilar-dbi.R`). In PostgreSQL, the read of the table is the
same with any batch. The engine amortizes a pass among the aggregates of the
same `SELECT`. What grows with the batch is the spill to disk of PostgreSQL.
The optimum depends on `work_mem`, which changes by server. To choose another
value, `instrumentar = TRUE` publishes the duration of each query.

If a batch fails, the batch is not lost. Its halves are probed by bisection:

- the accepted groups are reused as measurements;
- the culprit columns are retried by metric, with their local denominator;
- what still fails stays `no_disponible` with its reason.

If the budget runs out before isolating everything, the pending columns stay
unmeasured. They are not assumed to be culprits or readable.
`meta$tamano_lote_funciono` keeps the largest batch accepted in that run. No
state tied to the connection is kept.

`resumen_tabla$sql` adds `lote` and `columnas_compartidas` to see which query
was shared. The order of degradation is:

1. flat aggregates;
2. total of the universe, when needed;
3. distinct values;
4. mode;
5. median.

## Cost policy {#cost-policy}

The mode and the median are the expensive metrics. `politica_costo` (*cost
policy*) accepts `r length(eval(formals(perfilar_dbi)$politica_costo))` values,
and no other:

```{r politica-invalida}
tryCatch(
  perfilar_dbi(con, "tramites", politica_costo = "ninguna"),
  error = function(e) writeLines(strwrap(conditionMessage(e), 88))
)
```

- `"todas"` (*all*, the default) keeps mode and median in all the requested
  columns. The package does not choose for the user.
- `"por_cardinalidad"` (*by cardinality*) first resolves the structural
  sources: a guaranteed primary key says how many distinct values there are
  without counting them. It measures `validos` and `distintos` only if needed
  and if the strategy allows it. Then it omits, per column, **only the mode**,
  when `n_distintos / n_validos >= umbral_cardinalidad`. The threshold is
  `r codigo(lupa:::.UMBRAL_CARDINALIDAD_COSTO_DBI)` by default
  and can be moved in each call. The median is not omitted by cardinality: its
  cost is governed by the rows.

```{r por-cardinalidad}
barato <- perfilar_dbi(con, "tramites", politica_costo = "por_cardinalidad")
s <- sql_perfil(barato)
s[s$estado == "omitido_por_costo", c("columna", "metrica", "estado")]
writeLines(strwrap(barato$resumen_tabla$meta$decisiones_costo$monto$detalle$motivo, 88))
```

On a wider table, the difference shows in the number of queries. The table that
follows has 200 rows and 158 columns:

- numeric: 60;
- text: 60;
- integer: 20;
- dates stored as text: 18.

It is the same one that `benchmark/medir_plan_ancho.R` and
`benchmark/medir_politica_costo.R` use:

```{r tabla-ancha}
set.seed(1)
filas <- 200
generar <- function(prefijo, k, valores) {
  stats::setNames(lapply(seq_len(k), function(i) valores()), paste0(prefijo, seq_len(k)))
}
ancha <- as.data.frame(c(
  generar("num", 60, function() round(stats::rnorm(filas) * 100, 2)),
  generar("txt", 60, function() sample(letters, filas, replace = TRUE)),
  generar("ent", 20, function() sample(seq_len(50L), filas, replace = TRUE)),
  generar("fec", 18, function() {
    as.character(as.Date("2026-01-01") - sample(seq_len(900L), filas, replace = TRUE))
  })
))
DBI::dbWriteTable(con, "ancha", ancha)

corrida <- function(politica) {
  perfilar_dbi(
    con, "ancha", bloque_muestra = "solo_agregados", instrumentar = FALSE,
    politica_costo = politica, proteger_datos_personales = FALSE
  )
}
emitidas_ancha <- function(x) x$resumen_tabla$meta$consultas$emitidas
todas <- corrida("todas")
por_cardinalidad <- corrida("por_cardinalidad")
por_politica <- c(
  todas = emitidas_ancha(todas),
  por_cardinalidad = emitidas_ancha(por_cardinalidad)
)
por_politica
```

```{r comprobar-politica, echo = FALSE}
modas_omitidas <- with(sql_perfil(por_cardinalidad),
                       sum(metrica == "moda" & estado == "omitido_por_costo"))
stopifnot(modas_omitidas == por_politica[["todas"]] - por_politica[["por_cardinalidad"]])
```

With `"por_cardinalidad"`, the run saved
`r chartr(".,", ",.", num(por_politica[["todas"]] - por_politica[["por_cardinalidad"]]))`
of `r chartr(".,", ",.", num(por_politica[["todas"]]))` queries, all of them of
mode.

The structural sources are resolved whenever the policy needs the cardinality,
even if `estrategia_distintos` is omitted or not available. The strategy decides
whether it can be measured, but does not hide a guaranteed primary key. If there
is no structural source and the strategy does not allow measuring, the
cardinality stays unknown. Then the policy follows its rule for that case.

Each omission stays in `resumen_tabla$sql` as `omitido_por_costo` (*omitted for
cost*). It says what was omitted, why and how to request it again
(`politica_costo = "todas"` or another threshold). `meta$decisiones_costo`
explains separately the decision on each metric of each column.

`fuente_cardinalidad_costo` says where the proportion came from, and is
independent of `estrategia_distintos`. The policy never turns a request
`"aproximada_motor"` or `"catalogo"` into an exact `COUNT(DISTINCT)`.

## ⏱ The plan before running {#plan}

`plan_perfilado_dbi()` emits only preparation queries:

- the schema;
- the capability probes;
- the catalog of the primary key;
- in PostgreSQL, its statistics.

It says how many queries the profiling would emit, of which class and with
which scope. It does not scan data to decide the cost.

```{r plan}
plan <- plan_perfilado_dbi(con, "tramites")
knitr::kable(as.data.frame(plan))
```

```{r comprobar-plan, echo = FALSE}
emitidas <- por_omision$resumen_tabla$meta$consultas$emitidas
stopifnot(emitidas >= attr(plan, "total"), emitidas <= attr(plan, "total_maximo"))
```

The cost is a **range**:

- `attr(plan, "total")` (`r attr(plan, "total")` here) counts the queries if no
  batch is rejected. With `politica_costo = "por_cardinalidad"`, it assumes that
  the mode whose cardinality is not known is omitted.
- `attr(plan, "total_maximo")` (`r attr(plan, "total_maximo")`) adds the path
  that runs that mode and the bisection probes, if the engine rejected every
  batch. They are up to `2n − 1` per batch of `n` columns.
  `total_lotes_rechazados` publishes the same number.

The default run of the example emitted `r emitidas`.

The range holds when the sampling can be built. If
`universo = "muestra_motor"` and the form cannot be built,
`attr(plan, "muestreo")` declares it and the plan excludes those metrics. In
status `"no_sondeado"` (*not probed*), the form was only built locally. The
range stays conditional on the probe of the run accepting it.

The plan counts what `max_consultas` and `meta$consultas$emitidas` count: every
statement the profile sends to the engine, except the transaction guard and the
`pg_stat_statements` reads of `instrumentar`. With `bloque_filas` it counts the
preparation, the scan and the queries that follow; those the data ask for —the
median of a decimal whose central values are distinct doubles, its centred
standard deviation, the retry of a short `TABLESAMPLE`— go to `total_maximo`.
With `max_consultas = attr(plan, "total_maximo")` no metric is left out by the
budget.

The count follows the composition of the table, not the number of columns. With
the wide table of the previous section and one of 158 columns, all of them
text:

```{r plan-ancho}
plan_ancho <- plan_perfilado_dbi(con, "ancha")
recorre <- !as.character(plan_ancho$alcance) %in% c("una vez", "lee las filas pedidas")
texto <- as.data.frame(generar("txt", 158, function() sample(letters, filas, replace = TRUE)))
DBI::dbWriteTable(con, "ancha_texto", texto)
c(
  ancha = attr(plan_ancho, "total"),
  ancha_recorren_la_tabla = sum(plan_ancho$n_consultas[recorre]),
  solo_texto = attr(plan_perfilado_dbi(con, "ancha_texto"), "total")
)
```

Of the `r chartr(".,", ",.", num(attr(plan_ancho, "total")))` queries of the
wide table, `r chartr(".,", ",.", num(sum(plan_ancho$n_consultas[recorre])))`
scan, sort or group the whole table. Text columns cost less, above all because
the median —which sorts the table— is requested only on numeric columns.
`muestra` bounds none of that: it bounds what is brought into R, not the work
of the engine. `benchmark/medir_plan_ancho.R` redoes these figures and leaves a
dated output with the environment.

Each capability probe spends a fixed number of queries even if it succeeds with
the first form. It is a design decision. If the cost varied by engine, the plan
could not say exactly how many queries it is going to emit.

Counting queries does not say how much they cost: 14 queries on 2 million rows
are more work than 200 on 1,000. The plan also estimates the **magnitude**, in
2 halves:

- the one of the engine: `filas_leidas` and `ordenaciones_completas`,
  summarized in `magnitud_motor`;
- the one of the client: `columnas_texto` and `pares_texto`, summarized in
  `magnitud_texto`. `pares_texto` are the pairs of forms that the vocabulary
  detector could compare in R on the sample.

`magnitud` (*magnitude*) is the larger of the 2: `"baja"`, `"media"`, `"alta"`
(*low*, *medium*, *high*), or `"desconocida"` (*unknown*) if the number of rows
is not known. The plan does not count rows. Only in PostgreSQL, a positive
`pg_class.reltuples` provides a catalog estimate, labeled as such. In SQLite it
stays unknown:

```{r magnitud}
attr(plan, "magnitud")
num(attr(plan, "pares_texto"))
```

The magnitude is an estimate:

- the one of the engine counts the rows that would have to be read if no index
  helped;
- the one of the client counts pairs. Its cost depends on the length of the
  values, which the plan does not know without reading them.

Printing the plan shows the 2 halves, the high-work warning and the levers to
bound it. That text cites reference speeds of other runs to turn counts into
seconds. They are assumptions of the code, not measurements of the table.

The plan does not project seconds for `COUNT(DISTINCT)`: without reading data it
has no measured reference. With `universo = "muestra_motor"`, the plan also
declares the local copy:

- `attr(plan, "materializacion")`: the single selection that will be paid, with
  `pagado = FALSE`;
- `attr(plan, "pasadas")`: the passes that will read that copy.

## ⚠️ Cost and spill warnings {#warnings}

The warnings of `perfilar_dbi()` also arrive in non-interactive scripts,
because the cost is paid on the server. Each one has its switch and its
threshold. Turning it off does not turn off the measurement or its metadata.

| warning | how it projects | when it warns | where it stays |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `COUNT(DISTINCT)` | median of the durations of the first batch of distinct values of this run, times the number of batches | after the first batch and before the second, if there is more than one and the projection reaches `umbral_segundos_aviso_distintos` | `meta$costo_distintos` |
| mode | ms per distinct value of the first mode measured, times the cardinality of the others | before the next mode | `meta$costo_moda` |
| median | ms per row of the first median measured | before the pending medians | `meta$costo_mediana` |
| estimated spill (PostgreSQL) | size of the hash with `pg_stats` and `pg_class.reltuples` against `work_mem` | before the first `COUNT(DISTINCT)` | `meta$estimacion_derrame` |

The `r length(umbrales_aviso)` time thresholds are
`r lupa:::.UMBRAL_SEGUNDOS_AVISO_DISTINTOS_DBI` seconds by default, and `Inf`
turns off each warning explicitly. With a single batch of distinct values there
is nothing to project. The projection of distinct values does not use
`reltuples`. If the mode has no cardinality, the projection declares it instead
of assuming it.

```{r comprobar-umbrales, echo = FALSE}
# What the paragraph above states: every time threshold of the signature has
# the same default value.
omision_aviso <- vapply(umbrales_aviso, function(argumento) {
  eval(formals(perfilar_dbi)[[argumento]], asNamespace("lupa"))
}, numeric(1))
stopifnot(
  length(umbrales_aviso) > 0L,
  all(omision_aviso == lupa:::.UMBRAL_SEGUNDOS_AVISO_DISTINTOS_DBI),
  lupa:::.UMBRAL_SEGUNDOS_AVISO_MODA_DBI == lupa:::.UMBRAL_SEGUNDOS_AVISO_DISTINTOS_DBI,
  lupa:::.UMBRAL_SEGUNDOS_AVISO_MEDIANA_DBI == lupa:::.UMBRAL_SEGUNDOS_AVISO_DISTINTOS_DBI
)
```

```{r costo-distintos}
costo <- por_omision$resumen_tabla$meta$costo_distintos
str(costo[c("disponible", "n_lotes")])
writeLines(strwrap(costo$fuente, 88))
```

When a total median does not leave a local measurement, the projection uses a
reference of `r lupa:::.REFERENCIA_BANCO_MEDIANA_MS_POR_MILLON_FILAS_DBI` ms
per million rows. It is a constant of the code taken from another run, with no
script that redoes it. It is not presented as a measurement of the current run.
If the query that counted the rows was measured and gives a larger bound, that
bound is published separately, as an observed reading.

In PostgreSQL, the preparation also reads:

- `pg_stats.n_distinct` and `pg_stats.avg_width`;
- `pg_class.reltuples`;
- `work_mem` and, since PostgreSQL 13, `hash_mem_multiplier`.

If the estimated hash exceeds the effective limit, it warns that raising
`work_mem` in the session can avoid the spill. The package does not change the
configuration or wait for confirmation.

The estimate of the mode uses `EXPLAIN (FORMAT JSON, COSTS OFF)` without
`ANALYZE`. The one of the median models a sort with minimums of 32 bytes per
value for fixed types and 42 for `numeric`.

With `instrumentar = TRUE` and `pg_stat_statements` available, the measured
spill —temporary blocks written and read— prevails over the estimate. If the
call cannot be attributed, the status stays not available: the elapsed time is
not presented as evidence of spill.

The block `perfil_muestra` goes through `perfilar()`, and in an interactive
session it also receives its wide-table warning.

### Wide tables {#wide-table-warning}

```{r tabla-ancha-aviso-cifras, include = FALSE}
costo_ancho <- ajustado$meta$costo_tabla_ancha
umbral_celdas <- costo_ancho$umbral_celdas
velocidad_celdas <- costo_ancho$celdas / costo_ancho$duracion_estimada_segundos
stopifnot(
  abs(velocidad_celdas - lupa:::.VELOCIDAD_REFERENCIA_TABLA_ANCHA) < 1e-6,
  velocidad_celdas <= ancho_minima
)
```

Before starting the expensive stages, `perfilar()` projects how long a table can
take from its number of cells. From
`r chartr(".,", ",.", num(umbral_celdas))` cells it warns of the estimated
duration, only in an interactive session.
The projection is always kept:

```{r tabla-ancha-aviso}
str(ajustado$meta$costo_tabla_ancha[c(
  "celdas", "duracion_estimada_segundos", "umbral_celdas"
)])
```

The duration comes from dividing the cells by a reference speed of
`r chartr(".,", ",.", num(velocidad_celdas))` cells per second. It stays below
the slowest measurement of `benchmark/medir_referencias.R`:
`r chartr(".,", ",.", num(round(ancho_minima)))` cells per second, with 500 rows
and numeric and categorical columns.

It is a reference for the common case, not a bound.
`benchmark/medir_topes_valores_ancho.R` measures equal columns of text codes
(`"valor_1"`, `"valor_2"`...), with the near-duplicate search of the vocabulary
turned off. As all the columns are equal, the profile publishes a single
`columnas_duplicadas` finding that names them all. Its slowest case is `r chartr(".,", ",.", num(round(codigos_minima)))` cells per
second, also above the reference.

```{r codigos-ancho-comprobar, echo = FALSE}
stopifnot(codigos_minima > velocidad_celdas)
```

The 2 CSV files, in `benchmark/datos/`, keep the date, the environment and the
fingerprint of the code. The warning is turned off with
`avisar_costo_tabla_ancha = FALSE`, and `umbral_celdas_aviso_tabla_ancha = Inf`
is the same decision, explicit.

The dated measurements of wide tables are in
[Evidencia y rendimiento](https://sebollin.github.io/lupa/articles/evidencia-y-rendimiento.html#tablas-anchas)
(*Evidence and performance*, in Spanish). They are the query plan of an
administrative table of 158 columns and the 2 tables of speed.

## Instrumentation and durations {#instrumentation}

With `instrumentar = TRUE` (the default in the run), each row of
`resumen_tabla$sql` adds these fields:

- `duracion_ms`, which uses `Sys.time()`;
- `cpu_ms`, which adds `proc.time()[c("user.self", "sys.self")]` and measures
  the CPU work of the client, including the conversion of the result that the
  driver does;
- `n_filas_resultado` and `bytes_resultado_r`;
- `consulta_id`, `etapa` and `nivel`.

A `0` is measured; an `NA`, not measured. With `instrumentar = FALSE` the same
queries are emitted in the same order, and those fields stay `NA`.

`duracion_ms` is the duration of the **query**, repeated in each row that query
produced. To add up, only the rows of `nivel = 1` (*level*) count, the first of
each `consulta_id`:

```{r niveles}
s <- sql_perfil(por_omision)
table(s$nivel, useNA = "ifany")
length(unique(stats::na.omit(s$consulta_id)))
```

```{r suma-segura, eval = FALSE}
sum(s$duracion_ms[s$nivel == 1], na.rm = TRUE)
```

There are 2 identifiers that answer different questions:

- `consulta_id` identifies the statement that produced each measurement within
  the run, and defines the consistency group.
- `id_consulta` identifies the data query: 2 metrics with the same value saw
  exactly the same rows. It does not depend on `instrumentar`, and it is `NA` in
  the mode and the median, which do not share rows with other metrics.

`memoria_trabajo` (*working memory*) classifies the working state of the engine
as `creciente` (*growing*), `acotado` (*bounded*) or `NA`.

`resumen_tabla$tiempos` gathers the large stages of the client in the same
unit. Those of `nivel = 1` are disjoint; those of a higher level are contained
in one of them:

```{r etapas}
por_omision$resumen_tabla$tiempos[, c("etapa", "nivel", "estado")]
```

In an interactive session, a bar advances against the queries that the plan
expects to emit. `options(lupa.progreso = FALSE)` turns it off and `TRUE`
forces it. It does not change any measured value.

## Processing memory {#memory}

`plan_perfilado_dbi()` does not estimate the processing memory in R, and
declares it:

```{r memoria}
memoria <- attr(plan, "memoria_procesamiento")
memoria$estado
writeLines(strwrap(memoria$motivo, 88))
```

The attribute keeps 2 things:

- the known magnitude of the work (rows, cells and text pairs), labeled as
  magnitude and not as consumption;
- references of other runs, which are fixed texts of the code.

```{r memoria-referencias}
names(memoria)
names(memoria$referencias)
```

Those references say how much it cost to bring the rows, how much to process
them in R and how much that varied between tables. They come from a single
run, dated 2026-08-28, against a remote production engine, and this repository
cannot redo it.

They are not a prediction for the table of the plan. They are not used to
estimate because they vary between tables of the same magnitude.
`print(plan)` shows them, and the figures with their source are in
[Evidencia y rendimiento](https://sebollin.github.io/lupa/articles/evidencia-y-rendimiento.html)
(*Evidence and performance*, in Spanish).

Seeing every row and holding them all in memory is not the same. There are 3
recipes, depending on what is needed:

| need | configuration |
| --- | --- |
| bounded aggregates, without rows in R | `universo = "muestra_motor"`, `muestra_motor = n`, `bloque_muestra = "solo_agregados"` |
| row-level findings | `muestra = n`, with `orden_muestra` if the read has to be reproducible, and the caps on cells and bytes |
| summary of the whole table without retaining it | `bloque_filas = n` |

## A run on production databases {#production-run}

Between 26 and 30 October 2026, an external team ran `perfilar_dbi()` on 8
production databases:

- PostgreSQL: 5 databases, from 9.3 to 13;
- SQL Server: 3 databases, 2008 R2 and 2016.

The machine had 121 GB of memory and R 4.5.2. They are figures of a single run,
with the version of those dates and on data that the repository does not have.
They are not redone from here and are not extrapolated to another machine.

| | Small tables, single path | Aggregates (`tabla_completa`) | Engine sample |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Median | 0.6 s | 12 s | 26 s |
| 99th percentile | 47 s | 1,822 s | 323 s |

There were 3,709 calls on 3,316 tables, and 3,693 finished fine. Another 3
finished with a warning. Of the remaining 13, 11 were cut by the maximum time
that the team set and 2, by an error of the process.
The median memory of a call was between 230 and 530 MB depending on the path.
On those profiles, `reportar()` took a median of 0.06 s and
`planificar_limpieza()`, 0.008 s.

The protection of personal data was measured on 3 tables of up to 100,000
rows, with the same call with and without `proteger_datos_personales = TRUE`.
It cost between 11% and 18% more time, with a memory between 5% lower and 11%
higher. Each of those calls drew its own engine sample, so the rows were not
exactly the same. The engine and the driver also take their share. The
protection is a cost in the low double digits, not a null cost.

The slowest parts of that run were fixed afterwards. Each fix was measured on a
local reproduction, not on those databases, and the run on them is still to be
repeated:

- the standard deviation in SQL Server, which went in one query per column,
  each one on the whole table, goes in batches ([Batched queries](#batches)): on
  a million rows and 27 numeric columns it went from 27 queries to 2, and from
  1.42 million logical reads to 105 thousand, with the same figures;
- the date columns in R before 4.6: 100,000 dates went from 171 s to 1.3 s in
  R 4.5.2;
- the very long texts: 700 rows of four 14 KB columns went from 23 s to 5 s;
- the engine sample, which could bring into R more than its budget: 200 rows of
  1.25 MB of text and binary reach the spool in 27 KB
  ([Caps on the read into R](#caps)).

The first three figures are in the `NEWS.md` entry of each fix.

The agreement of the figures with an SQL count written separately is in
[Evidencia y rendimiento](https://sebollin.github.io/lupa/articles/evidencia-y-rendimiento.html#contraste-contra-el-servidor)
(*Evidence and performance*, in Spanish).

## Consistency across queries {#consistency}

The aggregates are separate statements, and the table can change between them.
The summary publishes it:

```{r snapshot}
por_omision$resumen_tabla$meta$snapshot
writeLines(strwrap(por_omision$resumen_tabla$meta$nota_snapshot, 88))
```

The hard bounds are checked only within one statement:

- the frequency of the mode, against its control count;
- the distinct values, against the `n_validos_guard` of their own query.

If exact `n_validos` and `n_distintos` are inconsistent and come from different
statements, the coverage adds an `alcance_distinto` (*different scope*) row. Its
reason names the 2 statements. It is evidence that the table changed during the
run, not an accusation against the engine or the package. If an approximation
cannot bring the control count, the check is declared as not available.

With `universo = "muestra_motor"` and `bloque_muestra = "con_muestra"`, the
selection of the engine runs **only once**. It is kept in a local copy: a
temporary file of the R session (the *spool*). The whole profile reads that
copy and never samples the engine again.

On each reread, a closing record checks `muestra_id`, `snapshot_id`,
`orden_id`, `n_filas`, `bytes` and the checksum. A missing record publishes
`spool_incompleto:trailer_ausente`, and a checksum that does not match,
`spool_checksum_invalido`. The copy does not write to the connection or create
temporary objects in the engine:

```{r copia-local}
copia <- del_motor$resumen_tabla$meta$materializacion
str(copia[c("backend", "estado", "externo", "objetos_temporales_motor",
            "validado_relectura")])
```

Rereading the copy can cost more than asking the engine for the selection again
on each pass. It is chosen because it guarantees that every metric describes the
same rows. `snapshot_id` identifies the copy of the client, not a transactional
snapshot of the engine.

For a consistent read, the path can run inside a transaction opened by the
user. That user sets the isolation level the engine needs. The package never
sends `BEGIN`, `COMMIT` or `ROLLBACK`. Outside a transaction, it does not add
statements of that kind. The same holds for `plan_perfilado_dbi()`,
`perfilar_coleccion()` (*profile a collection*) and `relaciones_coleccion()`
(*collection relationships*).

| engine | inside a transaction |
| --- | --- |
| PostgreSQL | an error aborts the transaction, so each statement goes between its own `SAVEPOINT` and its `RELEASE`, with `ROLLBACK TO SAVEPOINT` if it fails |
| SQL Server | it can roll back the transaction on an error; the path measures `@@TRANCOUNT` and `XACT_STATE()` before and after each send and read, and if they change it raises `lupa_error_transaccion_dbi` |
| MySQL, MariaDB, SQLite | the error of a query does not abort the transaction |
| DuckDB | an error while preparing aborts it and there is no `SAVEPOINT`: a view that fails leaves the transaction aborted, and it has to be closed with `ROLLBACK` |

## Dialects and probes {#dialects}

Bounding rows is not standard SQL. Before emitting the aggregates,
`perfilar_dbi()` probes the engine with a query that returns no rows. It
chooses the first capability that the engine accepts:

```{r dialectos, echo = FALSE}
d <- lupa:::.dialectos_dbi()
knitr::kable(data.frame(
  dialecto = paste0("`\"", names(d), "\"`"),
  forma = vapply(d, function(x) x$descripcion, character(1)),
  motores = vapply(d, function(x) x$motores, character(1))
), row.names = FALSE)
```

```{r dialecto-resuelto}
dialecto <- por_omision$resumen_tabla$meta$dialecto
str(dialecto[c("nombre", "declarado")])
writeLines(strwrap(dialecto$sondas, 88))
```

If no capability works, the portable path remains, which bounds in the client
with `dbSendQuery()` and `dbFetch(n)`. There the exact median is declared not
available, instead of bringing half a table into memory. If the probe gets it
wrong, `dialecto =` (*dialect*) declares the capability without probing:

```{r portable}
portable <- perfilar_dbi(con, "tramites", dialecto = "portable",
                         bloque_muestra = "solo_agregados")
s <- sql_perfil(portable)
writeLines(strwrap(s$motivo[s$columna == "monto" & s$metrica == "mediana"], 88))
```

Each probe tries the same form that is emitted afterwards. A cheaper form is not
enough: an engine can accept a clause with a trivially false filter and reject
it without it. DuckDB does it with block sampling:

```{r sonda-enganosa}
probar <- function(sql) {
  tryCatch({ DBI::dbGetQuery(duck, sql); "aceptada" },
           error = function(e) "rechazada")
}
c(
  con_filtro_falso = probar("SELECT 1 FROM t TABLESAMPLE SYSTEM (10) WHERE 1 = 0"),
  sin_filtro = probar("SELECT 1 FROM t TABLESAMPLE SYSTEM (10)")
)
```

Other rules of the dialect:

- The subquery alias is written with `AS` or without it, depending on the
  engine. The column aliases go between quotes and are compared without case
  sensitivity, because there are engines that fold them.
- The median under `muestra_motor` uses a single CTE with `COUNT(*) OVER ()` and
  `ROW_NUMBER() OVER` in 2 cases: in the dialects without a consolidated or
  scalar form (MySQL, MariaDB, SQL Server with compatibility below 110) and in
  each column that cannot use the consolidated one (a `float8` of PostgreSQL,
  a column with extremes). It chooses the 2 central positions without dividing
  and, with extremes, averages them without overflowing within the same
  statement. Its probe repeats that construction on
  `SELECT 1.0 UNION ALL ... SELECT 4.0`, and requires `2.5` and a negative
  control that fails. The production table is not probed. With
  `dialecto = "portable"`, which has no row skipping, the median of the whole
  table also comes from that CTE.
- With the driver recognized, the syntax probes of other engines are not run.
  In SQL Server with `XACT_ABORT ON`, a statement that does not belong would
  abort the transaction.

## What the engine stores differently from R {#differences-with-r}

The SQL summary describes what the engine has in front of it, and sometimes it
is not the same as the table in R. The full detail is in the section «Lo que el
motor guarda distinto que R» of `?perfilar_dbi`. The known cases, with what the
package publishes:

| engine | what happens | what `lupa` publishes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| SQLite | it has no date type: a `Date` is stored as days since 1970 | without more information it describes it as a number; with `extended_types = TRUE` when connecting, the column is temporal and receives no quantitative aggregates |
| SQLite | a column of numeric affinity admits text, and RSQLite reads it as `0` | it counts with `typeof()` the values stored as text or blob and declares the divergence with that cause |
| DuckDB | `NaN` is a value: it counts as present and distinct, and `MAX` or `AVG` answer `NaN` | a metric answered with `NaN` stays `no_disponible` with its reason |
| SQLite, PostgreSQL, DuckDB | `Inf` and `-Inf` enter `MIN`, `MAX`, `AVG` and the median | the magnitude statistics are requested again on the finite values, as in `perfilar()` |
| PostgreSQL | RPostgres reads `0` in every `money` cell, and a `real` through its text | both are read converted in the engine; the conversion stays in `meta$lectura_convertida` |
| PostgreSQL 9.3 to 11, or `extra_float_digits <= 0` | the text of a `double precision` has fewer digits | the read decodes the 8 bytes of the value with `float8send()` |
| SQL Server | `datetimeoffset` can arrive converted to UTC by FreeTDS | the lost offset is not rebuilt; the corroboration leaves it as a divergence |
| SQL Server | `STDEV` accumulates in one pass and loses digits with large means | the standard deviation is requested on the values centered on the mean |
| SQL Server | it does not admit `COUNT(DISTINCT)`, `GROUP BY`, `ORDER BY` or `MIN`/`MAX` on `text`, `ntext`, `image`, `xml` and `geography` | those metrics stay `no_disponible` without sending the statement |
| any | the collation of the column groups values that R tells apart (`COLLATE NOCASE`, non-deterministic ICU, trailing spaces in SQL Server) | `meta$criterio_comparacion` and `meta$criterio_moda` declare it; the corroboration leaves it `no_corroborada`, not `divergencia` |
| any | 64-bit integers (or `HUGEINT` and `UHUGEINT` in DuckDB) or decimals that arrive as double from 2^53 | the magnitude metrics that depend on a value a double cannot represent stay `no_disponible` (`r sub(" y ", " and ", enumerar(setdiff(lupa:::.METRICAS_DE_MAGNITUD_DBI, "mediana")), fixed = TRUE)`). The median is published when its value is exact: with an odd count, if the middle value is below 2^53; with an even count, if both middle values lie between -2^52 and 2^52, which costs one more query on the full table. `perfil_muestra`, the sample read into R and `perfilar()` decide it from its middle values, which they see: it is published when they fit in a double. The mode is requested from the engine as exact text; the sample reads those columns as text and, with [`bit64`](https://CRAN.R-project.org/package=bit64), as `integer64` |
| any | a decimal with more digits than a double holds arrives as a double | on the full table and with blocks, the mean and the standard deviation come from the sum of the column and the sum of the squares of its differences from the mean, which the engine computes in the column's type and returns as text; with the sample read into R, the mean, the median and the standard deviation come from each value's text, and the block median from the middle values the engine returns as text; on the engine sample with `solo_agregados`, from the same sums, requested in the statement of the aggregates. The `perfil_muestra` standard deviation follows the rule of the doubles on every path: it is not published, it is listed in `perfil_muestra$meta$desvio_decimal_doble`, and the cross-check does not compare it (cause `decimal_doble`) |
| MySQL, MariaDB, SQL Server, PostgreSQL, DuckDB | `AVG(x * 1.0)` of a decimal is cut at the engine's maximum scale (30, 38), `PERCENTILE_CONT` interpolates in double, and averaging in R the doubles of two middle values is not exact | a decimal's median sums its middle values in the engine and R divides by how many there are: one query per decimal column |
| SQL Server | `CAST(x AS VARCHAR)` is `VARCHAR(30)`, and writes `money` with two decimals | the sample reads a decimal's text as `VARCHAR(48)` and `money` with `CONVERT(..., 2)` |
| DuckDB | `AVG(x * 1.0)` overflows with a `HUGEINT` from 10^37 or a `UHUGEINT` from 10^38 | the basics are requested again without the average; the mean stays `no_disponible` and the rest is judged as in any column |
| DuckDB | `PERCENTILE_CONT` interpolates a `DECIMAL` in its own scale and truncates, and the driver converts a decimal of more than 18 digits to a double that is not the nearest | the median of a `DECIMAL` goes by the sum of its middle values, read through its text |
| PostgreSQL | `PERCENTILE_CONT` interpolates `low + (high - low) * 0.5` in double | with an even count and middle values more than 2^53 apart, the median stays `no_disponible` (that of a `numeric` goes by the sum of its middle values and is published) |
| SQL Server | `decimal - literal` beyond 38 digits is rounded, and from compatibility level 110 a tie rounds away from zero | the center of a decimal's standard deviation never ends in 5 |
| SQLite | RSQLite returns `integer` or `integer64` depending on the values of each block | with `bloque_filas`, blocks are joined as `integer64` before counting distinct values, mode and median |
| SQLite | the window mean of the sample is a rounded double | the sum of squares subtracts `n * (mean - center)^2` |
| any | each engine adds up in its own way, and with values that cancel out the means differ between engines and from the one of R | the mean is requested as double where decimal arithmetic would cut it; the corroboration declares the difference |

The mean of `{1e16, 1, -1e16}` is 1/3. Each path computes it in its own way, and
none is taken as true:

```{r medias-que-se-cancelan}
cancelan <- data.frame(x = c(1e16, 1, -1e16))
DBI::dbWriteTable(con, "cancelan", cancelan)
DBI::dbWriteTable(duck, "cancelan", cancelan)
c(
  sqlite = DBI::dbGetQuery(con, "SELECT AVG(x) FROM cancelan")[[1]],
  duckdb = DBI::dbGetQuery(duck, "SELECT AVG(x) FROM cancelan")[[1]],
  r = mean(cancelan$x)
)
```

When the 2 blocks exist and differ beyond the tolerance, the corroboration
leaves the `divergencia` row with the 2 values.

In SQLite, the difference of the dates shows like this:

```{r fechas-sqlite}
fechas <- data.frame(f = as.Date("2019-03-01") + 0:9)
perfilar_fechas <- function(...) {
  base <- DBI::dbConnect(RSQLite::SQLite(), ":memory:", ...)
  on.exit(DBI::dbDisconnect(base))
  DBI::dbWriteTable(base, "fechas", fechas)
  x <- perfilar_dbi(base, "fechas", bloque_muestra = "solo_agregados",
                    proteger_datos_personales = FALSE)
  columnas(x)[, c("columna", "minimo", "maximo", "media")]
}
perfilar_fechas()
perfilar_fechas(extended_types = TRUE)
```

## The primary key by engine {#primary-key}

The primary key is not guessed: it is read from the catalog of the engine. That
metadata query does not go through the table, and it is done in every run, with
any cost policy. The answer stays in `resumen_tabla$meta$clave`, with
`columnas`, `fuente`, `motivo`, `garantia` and `estado`. `garantia`
(*guarantee*) is `garantizada` (*guaranteed*), `declarada_no_garantizada`
(*declared, not guaranteed*), `desconocida` (*unknown*) or `no_declarada` (*not
declared*). A failed query keeps its reason and is not confused with a table
without a key.

With an unqualified name, the key published is the one of the relation that the
engine resolves, with its same schema rules. A key whose columns are not among
the ones just measured is discarded whole, in any engine, and the reason is
given.

What each catalog can state:

| engine | catalog path | `garantizada` when |
| --- | --- | --- |
| PostgreSQL | `pg_catalog` | the constraint is enforced and validated, without child tables by inheritance (partitions do not count), it is not `DEFERRABLE` and its index is unique; otherwise, `declarada_no_garantizada` |
| MySQL | `information_schema` | `ENFORCED` is `YES` |
| Oracle | `all_constraints` | `STATUS` is `ENABLED`, it is `VALIDATED` and it is not `DEFERRABLE` (tested with a simulated engine) |
| SQLite | `pragma` | all the columns of the key are `NOT NULL`; otherwise, uniqueness among non-null values is guaranteed but the guarantee stays `desconocida` |
| MariaDB | `show_index` | never: the catalog does not expose a comparable status and the guarantee stays `desconocida` |
| SQL Server | `information_schema` | never: it stays `desconocida` |
| DuckDB | `duckdb_constraints` | never: it stays `desconocida` |

```{r claves}
crear <- function(conexion, sql) invisible(DBI::dbExecute(conexion, sql))
crear(con, "CREATE TABLE con_nulos (id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, x TEXT)")
crear(con, "CREATE TABLE sin_nulos (id INTEGER NOT NULL PRIMARY KEY, x TEXT)")
crear(con, "CREATE TABLE sin_clave (id INTEGER, x TEXT)")
crear(duck, "CREATE TABLE padron (id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, x VARCHAR)")
leer_clave <- function(conexion, tabla) {
  x <- perfilar_dbi(conexion, tabla, bloque_muestra = "solo_agregados")
  k <- x$resumen_tabla$meta$clave
  data.frame(tabla = tabla, columnas = paste(k$columnas, collapse = ", "),
             fuente = k$fuente, garantia = k$garantia)
}
rbind(
  leer_clave(con, "con_nulos"),
  leer_clave(con, "sin_nulos"),
  leer_clave(con, "sin_clave"),
  leer_clave(duck, "padron")
)
```

With `politica_costo = "por_cardinalidad"`, a guaranteed key says how many
distinct values its column has without counting them. The check of a key that
the user declares on data in memory (`perfilar(clave = ...)`) is in
[Leer un perfil](leer-un-perfil.html) (*Reading a profile*, in Spanish). The
key suggestions are there too.

## 🗄️ Tested engines {#tested-engines}

The matrix is assembled when the page is built, with the output of
`benchmark/verificar_motor.R`: the file `benchmark/datos/verificar-motor.csv`.
Each row is an engine of the same run, with:

- the engine and the version that the server reports;
- the R driver and its version;
- the result of each check: `ok`, or `fallo` (*failure*) with the message.

Below go the date of the run, the revision of the package measured and the
fixture. An engine that did not respond stays `no_medido` (*not measured*),
with its reason.

```{r ubicar-corrida, include = FALSE}
ruta_motores <- local({
  declarada <- Sys.getenv("LUPA_VERIFICAR_MOTOR_CSV", unset = "")
  if (nzchar(declarada)) return(declarada)
  dir <- normalizePath(".", mustWork = FALSE)
  for (i in 1:5) {
    if (file.exists(file.path(dir, "DESCRIPTION"))) {
      return(file.path(dir, "benchmark", "datos", "verificar-motor.csv"))
    }
    dir <- dirname(dir)
  }
  # Woven from another folder: the loaded source package.
  file.path(getNamespaceInfo("lupa", "path"), "benchmark", "datos", "verificar-motor.csv")
})
hay_corrida <- !is.na(ruta_motores) && file.exists(ruta_motores)
# The matrix is what this section publishes: without the run, the page is not built.
if (!hay_corrida) stop("No encuentro benchmark/datos/verificar-motor.csv.")
comprobaciones <- c("cinco_columnas", "dialecto", "media", "clave_primaria", "cobertura")
if (hay_corrida) {
  motores <- utils::read.csv(ruta_motores, stringsAsFactors = FALSE,
                             na.strings = "", check.names = FALSE)
  # Exactly these columns: the text counts the checks with `comprobaciones`,
  # and a new column of the script has to show up here.
  stopifnot(setequal(names(motores), c(
    "motor", "version_servidor", "controlador", "version_controlador", "fixture",
    "revision_paquete", "fecha", "estado_motor", "motivo", comprobaciones
  )))
  version_corta <- function(x) {
    vapply(x, function(v) {
      if (is.na(v)) return("—")
      m <- regmatches(v, regexpr("[0-9]+(\\.[0-9]+)+", v))
      if (length(m)) m else "—"
    }, character(1), USE.NAMES = FALSE)
  }
  medido <- motores$estado_motor != "no_medido"
}
```

```{r matriz-motores, echo = FALSE, eval = hay_corrida}
resultados <- motores[, comprobaciones]
resultados[!medido, ] <- "—"
version_controlador <- ifelse(is.na(motores$version_controlador), "",
                              motores$version_controlador)
knitr::kable(
  data.frame(
    motores$motor,
    version_corta(motores$version_servidor),
    paste(motores$controlador, version_controlador),
    paste0("`", motores$estado_motor, "`"),
    resultados
  ),
  col.names = c("motor", "servidor", "controlador", "estado", "cinco columnas",
                "dialecto", "media", "clave primaria", "cobertura"),
  row.names = FALSE
)
```

```{r motivos-motores, echo = FALSE, results = "asis", eval = hay_corrida}
cat(
  "Corrida del ", paste(unique(motores$fecha), collapse = ", "), " (UTC), sobre ",
  "la revisión ", codigo(unique(motores$revision_paquete)), " del paquete. ",
```
