```{r motivos-motores, echo = FALSE, results = "asis", eval = hay_corrida}
  "Fixture declarado por el guion: «", paste(unique(motores$fixture), collapse = "»; «"),
  "».\n\n", sep = ""
)
sin_medir <- !medido | motores$estado_motor == "fallo"
if (any(sin_medir)) {
  cat("Motivos de lo que no se midió o falló:\n\n")
  cat(paste0("- ", motores$motor[sin_medir], ": ", motores$motivo[sin_medir], "\n"),
      sep = "")
}
```

What `benchmark/verificar_motor.R` does:

- It is run from the root of the source code:
  `Rscript benchmark/verificar_motor.R [motores]`. Without arguments it goes
  through the `r length(matriz_guion)` engines of the matrix
  (`r sub(" y ", " and ", enumerar(matriz_guion), fixed = TRUE)`).
  With arguments, only the named ones.
- It loads the package from the source with `pkgload`, if available: it
  measures the code of the tree and not the installed package.
- It does not take an arbitrary connection: each engine has its connection
  written in the script. SQLite and DuckDB go in memory; the others, in local
  containers with their own ports. The passwords of MySQL, MariaDB and SQL
  Server are read from `LUPA_MYSQL_PWD`, `LUPA_MARIADB_PWD` and
  `LUPA_MSSQL_PWD`. For another server or another engine, its connection has to
  be added to the script or the checks repeated by hand.
- It writes the fixture in each engine, and profiles `tramites` with the call
  that follows this list. The fixture has 2 tables:
  - `tramites`, of 500 rows and 5 columns: identifier, document, category,
    amount and age with 20 missing values;
  - `padron`, with primary key `id_persona` declared `NOT NULL`.
- It makes `r length(comprobaciones)` checks:
  - that the summary has 5 columns;
  - that the dialect was resolved;
  - that the mean of `monto` of the engine matches the one of R on the same
    column, with relative tolerance of `1e-8`;
  - that the primary key of `padron` is read from the catalog as `id_persona`;
  - that `resumen_tabla$cobertura` is a table.
- It ends with a non-zero code if any check fails.

```{r llamada-verificar-motor, eval = FALSE}
perfilar_dbi(
  con, "tramites", muestra = 500L, analizar_dependencias = FALSE,
  duplicados_aproximados = FALSE, proteger_datos_personales = FALSE
)
```

It does not check how many metrics are computed or how many stay `no_aplica`,
nor does it time anything. The check of the mean holds for finite values of
ordinary scale, like those of the fixture. With `NaN`, infinities or sums that
lose precision, the engine and R do not match. That is declared by the
corroboration between blocks ([above](#not-translated)).

What is not in the run:

| case | status | source |
| --- | --- | --- |
| engine that rejects `LIMIT` (the case of SQL Server, whose real matrix does not exercise that rejection) | tested with a simulated engine | `tests/testthat/test-arreglos-dbi.R` |
| engine that folds the aliases to upper case, like Oracle, DB2, Firebird or Snowflake | tested with a simulated engine | `tests/testthat/test-arreglos-dbi.R` |
| engine that rejects a column (a LOB that the driver does not materialize, a per-column permission) | tested with a simulated engine | `tests/testthat/test-arreglos-dbi.R` |
| Oracle (`fetch_first`, `rownum`, `SAMPLE`) | tested with a simulated engine; without a run against the real engine | `tests/testthat/test-dialecto-oracle.R` |
| BigQuery | not tested | — |
| another engine compatible with DBI | not tested; it runs through the portable path | — |

The simulated engine is a subclass of the RSQLite connection. It intercepts the
queries and behaves like the engine it imitates. It tests that restriction, not
the engine. With another engine, another driver or another version, the function
runs and declares in the coverage what it could not measure. But its figures are
not checked against that engine.

## Partial failures and errors {#failures}

No block discards the other:

- If the sample is requested and the engine rejects its query, or the sample
  cannot be profiled, the result comes out anyway. It carries the full
  `resumen_tabla`, `perfil_muestra = NULL` and a `no_disponible` row in the
  coverage, with the reason and how to solve it. If it was not requested, the
  row says `no_solicitado`, which is not a failure.
- If the engine rejects a column, its metrics stay `no_disponible` and the
  others are profiled whole. If the read of the sample fails, the culprit
  column is searched for by reading the same rows with fewer columns. An
  `alcance_distinto` row names it.
- A column that the credential cannot read, because of a per-column permission,
  is recognized in the catalog before reading. `has_column_privilege()` does it
  in PostgreSQL and `HAS_PERMS_BY_NAME()` in SQL Server. That column shows up
  with its metrics in `no_disponible` and is not named in any query.
- With dynamic masking of SQL Server and a credential without `UNMASK`,
  completeness is published. What depends on the value stays `no_disponible`.
- If a view fails on a row under `muestra_motor` or `bloque_filas`, the path
  tries the same summary on the whole table. The sample or the pass stay
  declared as `no_disponible`.
- With odbc, under a locale that is not UTF-8, a column name with an accent is
  not sent: the column stays `no_disponible`. The details of encoding are in
  [Codificación y locales](https://sebollin.github.io/lupa/articles/codificacion-y-locales.html)
  (*Encoding and locales*, in Spanish).

The errors of the path carry their own class, to catch them with `tryCatch()`.
All of them inherit from `lupa_error_dbi`:

- `lupa_error_conexion_dbi`;
- `lupa_error_tabla_dbi`;
- `lupa_error_campos_dbi`;
- `lupa_error_conteo_dbi`;
- `lupa_error_esquema_dbi`;
- `lupa_error_codificacion_dbi`;
- `lupa_error_argumento_dbi`;
- `lupa_error_transaccion_dbi`.

```{r clases-de-error}
error <- tryCatch(perfilar_dbi(con, "no_existe"), error = function(e) e)
class(error)
```

## Dependencies and installation {#dependencies}

`lupa` has `r length(dependencias("Imports"))` required dependencies,
`r sub(" y ", " and ", enumerar(dependencias("Imports")), fixed = TRUE)`.
It does not import any of them into its namespace: it calls them with `::`. It
is deliberate: `data.table` decides the meaning of `[` depending on whether the
calling package imports it. With the import in place,
`tabla[, columnas, drop = FALSE]` would stop selecting columns in the functions
that receive a table from the user.

`data.table` is used for 3 things:

- **Counting exact duplicate rows.** From
  `r lupa:::.UMBRAL_FILAS_DATA_TABLE_DUPLICADOS` rows, the count uses
  `data.table::frank()` with dense ranks. It falls back to `duplicated()` of
  base, which is the one that sets the result, in these cases:
  - list or compound columns;
  - `NaN` in double columns;
  - a `duplicated()` method of its own;
  - a numeric rounding setting of `data.table` in the session that is not exact
    (`setNumericRounding()`).
- **Copying `data.table` inputs before selecting columns.** A table of that
  class is copied to a `data.frame` with `data.table::copy()`, so the `[` that
  runs is the one of base.
- **Returning a usable `data.table` in remediation.** `aplicar()` copies the
  input, keeps the key (`setkeyv()`) and restores the column reserve
  (`setalloccol()`). That way the result is still a sound `data.table`.

The suggested ones are
`r sub(" y ", " and ", enumerar(dependencias("Suggests")), fixed = TRUE)`. In
the DBI path these take part:

- `DBI`;
- the driver of each engine (`RSQLite`, `duckdb`, `RPostgres`, `odbc`);
- `bit64`, which allows reading 64-bit integers in the sample without losing
  values.

The drivers of other engines (`RMariaDB`, `RMySQL`, `ROracle`, `bigrquery`) are
installed separately.

The hard case is not the R package but the system library underneath.
`RMariaDB` does not compile without the headers of the MySQL or MariaDB client,
and `ROracle` needs the Oracle Instant Client. `requisitos_motor()` (*engine
requirements*) says so before running into it.

```{r requisitos-cifras, include = FALSE}
catalogo_motores <- requisitos_motor()
# The catalog does not mark which entries are generic: the list belongs to this
# page, and each one is checked to exist.
genericas <- c("dbi", "odbc", "otro_dbi")
stopifnot(all(genericas %in% catalogo_motores$id_motor))
```

Its catalog has `r nrow(catalogo_motores)` entries:
`r sum(!catalogo_motores$id_motor %in% genericas)` for named engines and
`r length(genericas)` generic ones. The
`r sum(catalogo_motores$motor == "Oracle")` versions of Oracle count separately.
The generic ones (`r sub(" y ", " and ", enumerar(genericas), fixed = TRUE)`)
are not measured engines.

```{r requisitos}
r <- requisitos_motor()
knitr::kable(r[, c("id_motor", "motor", "version", "paquete_r", "dialecto",
                   "estado_prueba")], row.names = FALSE)
```

Each entry also declares the system library and its package in Debian and in
Fedora. If there is a way out without administrator rights, it declares it too:

```{r sin-administrador}
writeLines(strwrap(requisitos_motor("sql_server")$alternativa_sin_administrador, 88))
```

`requisitos_motor()` does not claim to have checked a system library that it
cannot check. In that case, its status is `no_comprobada` (*not checked*).

`estado_prueba` (*testing status*) is a declaration of the catalog, with its
source in `fuente_estado`. `esperado` (*expected*) means that the dialect is
built and tested against a simulated engine that reproduces its restriction,
not against the real engine. The evidence against each engine is the run of
[Tested engines](#tested-engines).

The columns that depend on the machine —whether the R package is installed— are
computed when called and are not shown here.

## Threads {#threads}

The work that can be parallelized uses **2 threads by default**
(`getOption("lupa.nucleos", 2L)`), the cap that CRAN asks to respect. It is
raised per call with `nucleos = 8` (*cores*), or for the whole session with
`options(lupa.nucleos = 8)`. The value is limited to the available cores and
stays published in `alcance$nucleos_usados`. The result does not change, only
how long it takes.

The threads govern the text comparisons that are delegated to `stringdist`.
They are those of:

- `detectar_duplicados_aproximados()`;
- `estimar_costo()` (*estimate cost*);
- `perfilar()` when approximate duplicates are requested, also for
  `perfil_muestra` through `...`.

The exact count of duplicate rows uses the thread configuration of
`data.table` itself (`data.table::setDTthreads()`), which the package does not
change.

[Escala y duplicados](escala-y-duplicados.html) (*Scale and approximate
duplicates*, in Spanish) explains how to choose the number of threads. The times
measured by number of threads, with their date and their environment, are in
[Evidencia y rendimiento](https://sebollin.github.io/lupa/articles/evidencia-y-rendimiento.html)
(*Evidence and performance*, in Spanish).

```{r cierre, include = FALSE}
DBI::dbDisconnect(con)
DBI::dbDisconnect(duck, shutdown = TRUE)
options(.opciones_previas)
```

:::
